record.context_brief: Maximum number of MOLS for arbitrary order
record.original_question: For an arbitrary order N, determine the maximal possible number of mutually orthogonal Latin squares. A Latin square of order N is an N×N array using N copies of N symbols with no repeated symbol in any row or column, and a set of mutually orthogonal Latin squares consists of Latin squares whose pairwise ordered symbol pairs occur exactly once; at most N−1 such squares can exist, prime-power orders attain this bound, but the general maximum remains open.

evidence.quote: A Latin square of order N is filled with N copies of N symbols arranged in a square in such a way that no row nor column of the square contains the same symbol twice.

A set ofk Latin squares which are pairwise orthogonal are called mutually orthogonal Latin squares(MOLS). It is easy to show that for a givenN there exist no more thanN− 1 MOLSs. Similarly with the case of the MUBs, this bound is saturated ifN is a prime or a power of a prime [80].
In general, the problem of finding the maximal number of MOLS for an arbitrary value ofN remains open [83].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Latin square of order N is an N×N array filled with N symbols such that each symbol occurs exactly once in every row and exactly once in every column. Two Latin squares L = (l_{ij}) and M = (m_{ij}) of order N are said to be orthogonal if the N^2 ordered pairs (l_{ij}, m_{ij}), as (i,j) ranges over all positions, are all distinct. A set of Latin squares of order N is called mutually orthogonal (MOLS) if every two of them are orthogonal. Let N(n) denote the maximum size of a set of MOLS of order n. It is classical that N(n) ≤ n−1 for all n ≥ 2, with equality whenever n is a prime power.

Determine N(n) for arbitrary n. In particular, give a formula or characterization of the maximal number of mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order n for every positive integer n that is not a prime power.
artifact.status_search_result: Determining the maximum number N(n) of mutually orthogonal Latin squares for general (non prime-power) order n is a long-standing open problem in combinatorial design theory. Only the upper bound N(n) ≤ n−1 (attained for prime powers), partial values for small n, and asymptotic lower bounds such as N(n) ≥ n^{1/17} − 2 for large n are known. The exact value remains unknown even for n = 10, 12, and many other small composite orders.

status_evidence.title: Mutually orthogonal Latin squares - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: N(n) = n−1 if n is a prime power; for large n, N(n) ≥ n^{1/17} − 2; exact values for general n remain unknown.
status_evidence.claim: The exact maximum N(n) is known only for prime powers and a few small orders; the general problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Concerning the number of mutually orthogonal Latin squares
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bounds on N(n) for composite n.
status_evidence.claim: Improved lower bounds exist but no general formula for N(n) is known.
